decisions.reason: The source changes post-mint modal wording, not FAQ content; the FAQ already describes random distribution of no-code rewards.
Changing the post-mint success message does not alter which NFT is minted or whether mint fulfillment succeeds.
The source assumes the existing random $5 commission and ticket distribution behavior and changes only the message shown after distribution.
The candidate governs referral-validation feedback stating what will happen, whereas the source specifies a separate post-transaction success modal stating what has happened.
The source does not change landing-page hero copy or its emphasized selling points.
The post-mint modal wording does not change certificate actions, email contents, or email availability.
The source repeats the existing $5 commission and prize-ticket outcome without changing the mint price or revenue allocation.
The source conditions the modal on rewards having been sent but does not change how commissions or tickets are recorded on accounting surfaces.
The source does not address Transak, fiat conversion, payment methods, wallet provisioning, or fiat mint delivery.
The source changes UI modal text and does not modify which attributes or counters must appear in NFT metadata.
Mentioning the NFT title and absence of a referral code does not change the mint-number-based referral identity or its display locations.
The random recipient in the source concerns no-code commission and ticket assignment, not selection of a prize-draw winner.
